paragraphs.source_en: In Ieyasu's eyes, victory in battle was far from enough; what mattered more was governing the realm. Rewarding merit, punishing wrongdoing, and redistributing domains—one problem after another would arise, and the slightest misstep could easily ignite fresh strife. The commander who had led one of the great armies at Sekigahara now had to become a ruler whose commands permitted no defiance, allowing no one the slightest objection to the wholly redrawn map of the realm...

paragraphs.source_en: Fukushima Masanori and Kuroda Nagamasa were, after all, their own men and therefore easier to persuade, but this placed both of them in an extremely awkward position. Though Ieyasu knew the entire course of events, he washed his hands of it completely, making it appear that Fukushima and the others, together with Ii and Honda, had conspired to deceive Mori Terumoto. Yet Terumoto and Ieyasu had still not reached a settlement, and the order had to be delivered.

paragraphs.source_en: “We had better leave this matter to Kuroda Kai-no-kami.” Fukushima Masanori stubbornly foisted the task of delivering the order onto Kuroda Nagamasa. paragraphs.source_en: Sure enough, Hiroie immediately sent a messenger back. Kuroda had his servants claim he was absent. paragraphs.source_zh: 果然，广家立刻就派了回使。黑田只好令人推说自己不在，未几，使者第二次求见，黑田又让人回说自己未归。但广家的使者第三次求见时，长政终于忍不住提笔给广家写了一封书函。

paragraphs.source_en: The affairs of the realm were cruel indeed. Nagamasa had originally mediated out of goodwill. Only now did he discover that the word “realm” allowed not the slightest place for private feeling; he had no choice but to act with merciless “impartiality.”

paragraphs.source_en: The other day, finding myself with no road left open, I had no choice but to appeal to you both for aid. Thanks to your unstinting assistance, the Naifu came to regard me in a new light. I shall never forget your kindness for all generations to come.
